title: Glycan shielding enables TCR-sufficient allogeneic CAR-T therapy
one_line: The episode covers a Cell paper proposing that engineered glycan shielding of donor cells allows allogeneic CAR-T products to retain their endogenous TCR rather than requiring TCR knockout.
key_claims: Glycan shielding is presented as an engineering strategy to protect allogeneic CAR-T cells from host immune rejection.
The approach is claimed to be 'TCR-sufficient', i.e. the endogenous TCR does not need to be deleted to avoid graft-versus-host complications in the allogeneic setting.
No specific quantitative results were available in the supplied show notes; numbers must be read from the source paper.
limitations: The show notes contain only a DOI, so no effect sizes, model systems, or control comparisons could be recorded here.
Whether glycan shielding durably prevents host rejection over long time courses, and in immunocompetent large-animal or human settings, is not established from the material provided.
Retaining the endogenous TCR raises GvHD and alloreactivity questions that the available material does not quantify.
open_questions: Head-to-head comparison of glycan-shielded TCR-intact allogeneic CAR-T versus TCR-knockout allogeneic CAR-T for persistence, GvHD incidence, and antitumour efficacy in a fully allogeneic immunocompetent model.
Does the glycan shield persist through repeated antigen encounter and cell division, or is it diluted or remodelled in vivo?
Clinical translation: can shielded products be manufactured from unmatched donors at scale without additional gene edits?
